content.theory:
# Day 01 — HTML Document Structure ## Learning objectives By the end of this lesson you will be able to create a valid HTML5 document and explain the role of each major section. ## What is HTML? HTML (HyperText Markup Language) describes the **structure** of a web page. The browser reads your HTML and builds a DOM (Document Object Model) tree. Styling comes later with CSS; behavior comes later with JavaScript. ## Minimum valid document ```html My First Page

Hello

This content is visible on the page.

``` ## Section roles | Part | Purpose | |------|---------| | `` | Declares HTML5 so the browser uses stinsideds mode | | `` | Root element; `lang` helps accessibility and SEO | | `` | Metadata: title, character set, CSS links (not visible) | | `` | Correct rendering for international characters | | `` | Text shown in the browser then and search results | | `<body>` | Everything the user sees | ## Tags, elements, and attributes - A **tag** is the markup itself: `<p>` or `</p>` - An **element** is the full unit: `<p>Hello</p>` - An **attribute** adds information: `lang="en"`, `charset="UTF-8"` ## Common mistakes - Putting visible text inside `<head>` - Forgetting `<title>` - Saving the file as `.txt` instead of `.html` ## Summary Master the skeleton first. Every future page starts from this structure.
content.notes:
# Day 01 — Quick notes

- Always start with `<!DOCTYPE html>`
- Put `charset` and `viewport` in `<head>`
- Visible content belongs only in `<body>`
- Prefer `index.html` as the home page filename

2. Type a full HTML5 skeleton without copying.
3. Set the title to your name and add one heading and one paragraph in the body.
4. Open the file in a browser and use View Page Source to verify the markup.

Create `day01-profile-shell.html` with a valid HTML5 skeleton, title “My Learning Journal”, an `h1` with your name, and a short paragraph about why you are learning frontend development. Commit: `day-01-html-structure`.
content.interview:
# Day 01 — Interview questions

**What does HTML stand for?** HyperText Markup Language.

**Why is DOCTYPE required?** It tells the browser to render in stinsideds mode as HTML5.

**What is the difference between head and body?** Head holds metadata; body holds visible content.

**Why use UTF-8?** So characters from many languages display correctly.
content.project:
# Day 01 — Mini project

Build a “blank learning hub” page with only structure: title, one `h1`, and two paragraphs. No CSS yet.
content.solution:
# Day 01 — Solution tips

If the page looks empty, confirm your text is inside `<body>` and the file extension is `.html`.
content.cheatsheet:
# Day 01 — Cheat sheet

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
 <meta charset="UTF-8" />
 <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
 <title>Page title</title>
</head>
<body></body>
</html>
```

/*
STEP 1: Project banao
npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react

STEP 2: Folder me jao
cd my-app

STEP 3: Packages install
npm install

STEP 4: Dev server chalao
npm run dev

Browser me http://localhost:5173 khulega

-------------------------------------------------
IMPORTANT FILES:

package.json     → dependencies aur scripts
vite.config.js   → Vite settings
index.html       → main HTML (yahan #root div hota hai)
src/main.jsx     → React app yahan se start hota hai
src/App.jsx      → main component
src/App.css      → styles
src/assets/      → images etc.
src/components/  → apne components yahan banao (khud folder banao)

-------------------------------------------------
main.jsx roughly aisa dikhta hai:

import React from 'react'
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client'
import App from './App.jsx'
import './index.css'

ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root')).render(
  <React.StrictMode>
    <App />
  </React.StrictMode>
)

- createRoot → React 18 ka naya API
- getElementById('root') → index.html ka div
- <App /> → tumhara main component
*/
